title: Kingdom Hearts' Composer Wrote Street Fighter II's Music First
hook:
Yoko Shimomura joined Capcom in 1988 against her teachers' advice, scored Street Fighter II in 1991, then moved to Square and wrote Kingdom Hearts' Dearly Beloved for a single cutscene. Which Kingdom Hearts track still lives in your head?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know the composer of Kingdom Hearts wrote the music for Street Fighter II first? Yoko Shimomura grew up on classical piano and studied music at college in Osaka. In 1988 she took a job at Capcom straight out of school. Her teachers and friends did not approve, and one professor told her to give up the idea. Three years later, in 1991, Capcom released Street Fighter II, and the arcade soundtrack that millions of players hummed was hers. She later called it her baby. In 1993 she left Capcom for Square, where she scored Super Mario RPG, Parasite Eve and Legend of Mana. Then in 2002 came Kingdom Hearts. Shimomura has said she does not really know why she was picked, and joked that her schedule just happened to be free. Her piano piece Dearly Beloved was written for an emotional cutscene. Instead it became the title theme, and a new version has opened almost every game in the series since. She later went on to score Final Fantasy XV. So the fighting game music of the arcades and the gentlest menu theme in gaming came from the same hands. Which Kingdom Hearts track do you still hear in your head? Follow for more gaming history.
